title: Deadline-tiered batch admissibility with KV-pressure mitigation
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Continuous batching improves GPU utilization by aggregating token generation requests, but long-running batches or heavy KV cache residency can cause tail latency violations for latency-critical customers. Current preemption strategies are either heavy-handed (global eviction of KV) or coarse-grained (tenant time-slices) and do not consider per-request deadlines or progressive KV pressure.

Goal: Implement a deadline-tiered admissibility controller that admits requests into in-flight batches based on a combination of per-request SLO deadline, estimated token budget, and current KV cache pressure. The controller should: 1) reduce tail latency violations for deadline-sensitive traffic, 2) avoid indiscriminate KV churn, and 3) maintain overall throughput and GPU memory utilization.

What success looks like (metrics):
- 50% reduction in P99 generation latency for requests tagged as latency-sensitive under mixed workloads.
- <10% increase in average per-token cost vs baseline continuous batching for same throughput.
- KV cache eviction rate reduced vs a naive LRU-evict-on-preempt approach (target: -30%).
- No more than 5% throughput regression for best-effort traffic in steady-state.
acceptance_criteria: Controller correctly classifies requests into deadline tiers and admits/rejects based on configurable thresholds
Admitted request flows receive bounded additional queuing delay; can demonstrate SLO attainment in canary traffic
KV eviction count and bytes evicted measured and reduced compared to baseline under the same mixed workload
Simulation harness + unit tests cover corner cases: sudden KV pressure spike, many concurrent latency-sensitive requests, GPU OOM avoidance path
Canary rollout strategy defined and exercised with rollback criteria (increase in client-side P99 or GPU OOMs)
design_decisions: Use a soft-admission policy that prefers delaying admission for best-effort requests instead of immediate KV eviction
Compute per-request admission score combining: time-to-deadline (TTL), estimated token budget, tenant priority weight, and KV pressure factor
KV pressure factor derived from real-time slab occupancy + recent eviction rate rather than raw free bytes to avoid oscillation
Admission thresholds are configurable by deployment tier (hosted vs dedicated) and dynamically tunable via runtime flags
Avoid global locks in the admission hot path; use read-copy-update style snapshots of KV occupancy metrics sampled at batch boundaries
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument runtime to expose KV slab occupancy and recent eviction rate metrics at batch boundaries (ENG-90723.1)
2) Add per-request metadata for deadline and estimated token_budget in the front-end SDK/ingress (ENG-90723.2)
3) Implement admission controller module with pluggable scoring formula and feature flags (ENG-90723.3)
4) Integrate controller with batch scheduler hot path; ensure fast-path uses snapshot metrics and early returns (ENG-90723.4)
5) Implement mitigation actions for declined admissions: redirect to best-effort queue, smaller micro-batches, or trigger KV soft-eviction only under sustained pressure (ENG-90723.5)
6) Add unit + integration tests and a simulator to model mixed workloads and KV dynamics (ENG-90723.6)
7) Canary rollout to small set of tenants with monitoring dashboards and rollback hooks (ENG-90723.7)
testing_plan: Create controlled simulator scenarios: high-latency-sensitive load + background long-run generation to validate P99 improvements
Fuzz admission thresholds and KV pressure signals to ensure stability and no oscillatory behavior
E2E tests that inject synthetic KV pressure and validate that controller prefers request delay over aggressive eviction
Load test on dedicated cluster to verify throughput/regression targets are respected
Run canary against 3 internal tenants for 48h with traffic mirroring before public rollout
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag. Stage 1: enable in canary region (us-west-2) on 10% of hosts.
Stage 2: expand to 30% hosts and adjust thresholds based on telemetry after 72h.
Stage 3: global rollout to hosted tier; enable opt-in for dedicated customers and provide configuration knobs.
Immediate rollback criteria: >10% increase in endpoint P99 for any latency-sensitive tenant, any GPU OOM observed, admission controller exceptions >0.1%.
Post-rollout: gradual tuning window (2 weeks) to adjust per-tenant weights and thresholds.
Documentation: update runtime config docs and console observability page with KV-pressure and admission metrics
monitoring_and_metrics: Per-tenant accepted/rejected admission counts and rates
Admission decision latency (ns) and CPU overhead in scheduler hot path
KV slab occupancy % (by slab size), eviction rate (bytes/s), and eviction count
P50/P95/P99 generation latencies split by deadline-tier
Per-token cost delta for affected tenants vs baseline
GPU memory headroom and OOM incident logs
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Admission scoring mis-calibration causes starvation of best-effort traffic -> Mitigation: add token-budget floor and proportional fairness windows
Risk: Oscillation between admitting and evicting KV -> Mitigation: use hysteresis and exponentially weighted moving average for KV pressure
Risk: Increased scheduler CPU latency -> Mitigation: keep admission computation O(1) and offload heavy arithmetic to sampling threads
Risk: Bad SDK clients not setting deadlines -> Mitigation: treat missing deadline as best-effort and expose clear docs + warning logs
alternatives_considered: Aggressive per-request KV eviction on preempt: simpler but causes high KV churn and quality regressions
Strict tenant time-slicing: predictable but poor utilization with mixed request sizes
Priority-only queue without deadline awareness: eases implementation but fails to capture urgency of short-deadline requests

2026-03-14 Lina Chen (SRE): Ran stress-tests on dedicated cluster; eviction rate improved but observed slight 2% throughput regression for best-effort. Will iterate on threshold tuning.
